review.verdict: The cast and joke concept are sound, but execution breaks down: the robot overlaps the human's head, the doorway sits empty and disconnected, the wire is nowhere near the bot's foot, and the bot/spill clip outside the safe area — this reads as a jumble, not a tripping gag, so it fails on composition and polish.
revisionNotes: The door (round speech-bubble doorway) sits empty at bottom-left, completely disconnected from the robot — move it to left-third at the bot's height so the robot is visibly passing through it, per the brief's 'left to right' staging.

The wire is anchored near the viewer's chair, not under the bot's trailing foot, so the 'tripped on a wire' beat is lost — reattach wire to bot's foot/leg anchor instead of offsetting toward the human.
Bot's legs directly overlap the viewer's head and torso — this is a polish-breaking overlap; separate the anchors so the bot trips in open space to the left of the chair, not stacked on the person.
Lint flags both 'bot' and 'spill' extending outside the safe area — scale bot down to ~0.85 and shift left, and pull the spill's flying items (currently clipped at x~1041) back inside the frame.
Reduce bot's rotate from 18° — combined with the 'arms out, surprised' pose and no visible ground contact, the robot reads as floating/flying rather than mid-trip.

Composition has no clear left-to-right read (door, wire, spill, chair are scattered with gaps and overlaps) — reflow so door → tripping bot → wire → spilled bags → viewer forms one legible diagonal line.

review.verdict: The riso-duotone palette is fresh and the cast casting is correct, but the spilled bag overlaps the human instead of the robot, the wire barely touches the trip point, and a large empty top half plus a chair/human render glitch make the joke take more than a glance to parse — needs a composition and placement pass before publishing.
revisionNotes: Spill component drifts into the viewer's space, overlapping the human's face/shoulder; pull its offset in toward the bot (e.g. offset [10,-60] instead of [30,-90]) so flying bag contents read as coming from the robot, not floating at the person.

Wire reads as a disconnected plug near the floor with a visible gap to the robot's feet; scale it to ~1.4 and re-anchor to bot's trailing foot (side: bottom, offset near [0,-5]) so the trip is legible.

Top ~40% of the frame is empty while all four elements crowd the bottom; raise door/bot/chair/viewer anchors upward (y from 0.6-0.82 toward 0.45-0.65) or add a simple floor/rug shape to balance the square.
Chair and viewer have an overlapping double-edge render glitch at the armrests; nudge chair x by -0.03 and drop its scale to ~0.9 so the silhouettes don't collide.
Doorway circle overlaps the bot's arm/antenna, making the speech-bubble shape hard to parse as a threshold; move door to x=0.16 and scale to 0.9 to open a clear gap between door and robot.
Viewer's arms-crossed, unimpressed pose from the brief doesn't register in the render; confirm the human component's pose prop reads as crossed arms, or add a small raw shape for folded arms.

review.verdict: The gag is legible on a close look but the execution undercuts it: the doorway is a bare floating circle disconnected from the bot, the trip and spill read ambiguously rather than as a clear stumble, and a leg/chair overlap looks like a rendering glitch, leaving the bottom third of the frame empty.
revisionNotes: Give the door real presence: thicken into a proper arched doorway (add a frame/threshold line) and move it to x~0.22 so the bot visibly passes through it; right now it's a bare circle floating in empty space, disconnected from the bot.
Tilt the bot further forward (rotate ~20-25 instead of 10) with front leg extended toward the wire, so the trip reads as a fall-in-progress, not a surprised stand still.

Reposition the wire directly under the bot's front foot (offset so it overlaps the leg, not sits below-left of it) so contact with the trip hazard is unmistakable; currently it reads as a stray power cord.
Redraw the spill props as a diagonal spray of items falling below-right of the bag rather than hovering above it, so it clearly reads as contents spilling, not confetti.
Fix the clipping between the chair's front-leg shape and the human's legs (currently a double-exposed leg artifact); nudge the human's x anchor or the chair leg props so they don't overlap.
Fill the empty bottom third of the frame: lower the y-anchors for door/bot/chair slightly and bump overall scale so the composition uses the full square instead of a thin horizontal band.
